name: Neal Aronson
forbes_bio: Neal Aronson is the founder and principal investor behind Roark Capital, which owns 30,000 sandwich shops of Subway, Jimmy John's, Arby's and Sonic.
Aronson has led Roark, named after the ruthlessly competitive architect in Ayn Rand's The Fountainhead, since he founded it two decades ago.
He remains the firm's majority owner.
Aronson is responsible for most of the restaurant industry's biggest deals of the past decade, among them Roark scooping up Carl's Jr. and Hardee's for $1.75 billion in 2013.
In December 2020, Roark spent $11.3 billion to acquire Dunkin? and Baskin-Robbins.

name: Martua Sitorus
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Martua Sitorus cofounded Wilmar with Kuok Khoon Hong, now also a billionaire, in 1991.
Sitorus stepped off the board of Wilmar, one of the world's largest palm oil traders, in 2018.
He and his brother Ganda cofounded KPN, formerly known as Gama, with interests in palm oil plantations, property development and cement manufacturing.
In partnership with the Ciputra Group, KPN's property arm Gama Land built a township in Medan, North Sumatra in 2024.
The family's cement maker Cemindo Gemilang listed its shares in 2021 raising $77 million. Their hospital company Murni Sadar raised $21 million through an IPO in 2022.
forbes_facts: A former economics student, Sitorus traded shrimp as a teenager, then switched to palm oil.
His business partner Kuok Khoon Hong is the nephew of revered Malaysian businessman Robert Kuok.

name: Bernard Broermann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2009-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2025)
forbes_bio: Bernard Broermann is the founder of Asklepios Kliniken GmbH, one of the three largest operators of private hospitals in Germany.
His first hospital opened in 1984, and the group now employs more than 50,000 people and has 170 hospitals and medical clinics worldwide.
Asklepios holds a majority stake in mediClin AG, a German operator of hospitals and clinics.
In May 2020, the Bundeskartellamt cleared Asklepios's planned acquisition of of rival hospital group Rhoen-Klinikum AG, in which it already held a stake; today it holds 91.75% of the group.
Broermann also owns five luxury hotels in Germany and Switzerland.
forbes_facts: Broermann, from a family of farmers, has M.B.A. degrees from Harvard University and INSEAD.
Before founding Asklepios, he practiced as an accountant and lawyer.

name: Gerry Harvey
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Gerry Harvey is cofounder and executive chairman of furniture and electrical goods chain Harvey Norman.
He also controls a property portfolio and owns the Magic Millions racehorse auction market.
He describes his wife Katie Page, who runs Harvey Norman, as "the mastermind" of the operation.
Page also holds shares in the company.
Harvey Norman has more than 100 company operated stores overseas, in countries like New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia, Slovenia and the UK.
forbes_facts: Harvey plans to open five Harvey Norman stores in Britain across England's West Midlands.

name: Ye Chenghai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: A politician turned entrepreneur, Ye Chenghai chairs Shenzhen Salubris Pharmaceuticals which makes cardiovascular, cancer and anti-infective drugs.
Ye was the mayor of Shenzhen in the 1980s.
Ye's son Kevin is Salubris' CEO; his daughter Ye Yujun is a board member.

name: Peng Lei
appears_on: Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2025)

name: David Grain
forbes_bio: David Grain is the CEO of Grain Management, a private equity firm he founded in 2007.
Grain Management is focused on broadband and communication infrastructure investments.
Before founding Grain Management, he led wireless infrastructure company Global Signal from bankruptcy to IPO.
Grain Management purchased 15 megahertz of spectrum in T-Mobile's 800 MHz band in 2025 and Quintillion, an Alaskan fiber-optic network, in 2024.
Grain and his wife founded the Grain Fellows Program in 2004, funding SAT and college prep, application fees and mentorship for low-income students at Booker High School in Sarasota, Florida.
forbes_facts: He is a lifetime member of the Council on Foreign Relations.
Grain was appointed by President Barack Obama to the National Infrastructure Advisory Council at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

name: Wichai Thongtang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2025)
forbes_bio: Lawyer-turned-investor Wichai Thongtang gets a substantial chunk of his fortune from a minority stake in hospital operator Bangkok Dusit Medical Services.
His son Att has a board seat at Bangkok Dusit.
Wichai's portfolio includes TWZ, a distributor of mobile phones and peripheral devices, and E For L Aim, a dealer of medical equipment and supplies.
He is chairman of listed Royal Orchid Hotel (Thailand) and Grande Asset Hotels And Property.
forbes_facts: He has represented former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra.
Wichai had a loss-ridden cable-TV company, which was shut down in 2016.

name: Daniel Hunt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Dan Hunt owns the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs with his three siblings. His brother Clark is chairman and CEO.
Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.
Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.
The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while Dan is president.
Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982.
